sourceRegistry.scope: Original MIT NetAtlas QX conversion code bundles ISC-licensed yaml 2.9.1 and an Apache-2.0 static script registry. All notices and complete licenses are retained. Separate optional pinned Maasea runtime artifacts retain Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause/CC0-1.0. Loon remains an external AGPL release recipe; no KOP-XIAO parser source is copied.
sourceRegistry.verification: QX conversion/helper tests execute the generated browser bundle in a restricted VM. A separate four-public-source gate checks original URLs and complete source bytes without evaluating downloaded business JavaScript. Loon retains verified upstream GET bytes and non-executing syntax review. Native application imports are not run.

quantumultX.author: NetAtlas contributors

sourceContract.input: QX $resource object with content and optional link/type; unknown type values are not guessed from numbers.
sourceContract.completion: Exactly one $done result and the same final evaluated object. Supported native results are content/error, opt-in numeric info, and one native user-agent retry with fallback content/error. Parser does not perform HTTP requests.
sourceContract.options: Resource-specific literal keyword selection, bounded Thompson-NFA regex/regout and declaration replacements, sequential naming/templates, ordering/duplicate controls, explicit native connection overrides, rule flags/policy/relay, rewrite destination selection, module arguments and opt-in local host utilities. Unknown or incompatible options fail atomically. No source JavaScript evaluation.
sourceContract.diagnostics: Rejected fields identify a fixed source-format context and a registered public schema name only. Arbitrary unknown key names and all source values are redacted; no subscription URL, credentials or node label are included.

nativeClientPreferences.behavior: Bounded strings use native QX behavior; fixed notices explain that client fingerprint preferences are not preserved and spx is omitted. No mode switch or source values in notices. Source input remains unchanged.
nativeClientPreferences.boundaries: SS/SSR URI, explicit SIP008 v1, sing-box and native QX fields remain strict; no certificate pin, verification, credential, endpoint, flow or transport field is dropped.

sourceFormats: Clash VMess/VLESS nested reality-opts with TLS enabled
nativeRealityCapabilities.behavior: A true hint is satisfied by the documented native QX Reality handshake. A fixed notice describes the capability, not the negotiated group. No extra native QX field or source value is emitted.
nativeRealityCapabilities.rejected: False, zero, empty, non-scalar or invalid values; non-Reality or misplaced fields; native QX, sing-box and explicit SIP008 including missing-id paths. pqv and certificate/signature settings remain strict.
nativeRealityCapabilities.requires: A QX version implementing the documented native iOS26 Reality handshake with X25519MLKEM768 support.

resourceLimits.unit: UTF-16 code units; normalized physical lines and unfiltered emitted rows are separately bounded
resourceLimits.structuredDocuments: Existing YAML/JSON depth, value-node and alias budgets remain unchanged; large plain-rule allowance does not apply to structured or encoded input.

rewriteResources.installationComments: Statically extracts explicit rewrite_local/mitm sections from leading JavaScript installation comments only. Business JavaScript is never evaluated; task_local examples are not installed.

domainConjunctions.conditions: Two to four positive flat DOMAIN/HOST exact, suffix or keyword predicates; exact glob intersection, not OR or source-row deletion.
domainConjunctions.budgetScope: One whole resource, including all mixed rewrite/filter chunks. Other logical/IP/port conjunctions fail atomically.

rewriteResources.foreignScriptDeclarations: Known, licensed, source-verified Maasea request/response sources compile to pinned static Surge-contract adapters. Module defaults and explicit JSON arguments, name, binary mode, byte limit and timeout are passed to the adapter. Unknown foreign sources with these parameters fail instead of dropping settings; parameter-free references retain an explicit unverified-API notice. script-compat=qx is a user declaration only.
rewriteResources.urlRegexReject: URL-REGEX REJECT converts to QX reject-200 response blocking with an explicit comment that connection-close semantics differ. Other URL routing policies fail.
rewriteResources.declarativeActions: Map Local inline text/tiny-gif/base64 responses preserve status/headers/bytes through a static script-echo-response adapter without upstream HTTP; JSON jq/del/replace and supported request/response header actions have effect tests.

apis: request/response text and exact byte views
HTTP callbacks via native QX fetch
source-path-scoped default storage key; explicit source keys retain names
scriptRuntime.limitations: No arbitrary source runtime rewriting, remote source eval, WebView, Surge control API or unregistered platform APIs. Byte limits run after native buffering; timers cannot preempt synchronous CPU; empty-body invocation remains native QX behavior. The pinned script runtime is a separate opt-in installed rewrite and can use host network/storage; the resource converter cannot.

nativeConnectionOverrides.domainVerification: cert=FQDN, e.g. cert=verify.example, emits tls-verification=verify.example. It is a verification hostname, not the literal word domain.
nativeConnectionOverrides.limitations: Ineffective or conflicting pins and transport overrides are rejected. tls13 is deprecated in current QX and does not disable TLS 1.3. uot=1 requests legacy Python UOT, not modern sp.v1/sp.v2. Reality ignores/rejects unsupported ALPN/session/TFO combinations.

regularExpressions.implementation: Original bounded Thompson NFA; no backtracking or user eval. Literal atoms, character classes, anchors, word boundaries, alternation, captures and non-nullable repeated groups are supported. Lookarounds, backreferences and repeated nullable groups are rejected.
regularExpressions.replacement: Standard string GetSubstitution tokens, including capture references, with shared work and output bounds. Literal rename patterns remain literal; templates expand only user-authored template positions, never source names/tags or captured source text.

ruleResources.automaticBareList: Mixed bare domains, IPv4/IPv6 and CIDRs; explicit DOMAIN-SET retains its exact/suffix format contract.
ruleResources.domainRegex: Exact bounded finite positive domain-regex to glob compilation plus registered native mappings; no widening fallback.
ruleResources.olderNotes: Portable preceding comment; never emit unsupported leading-note syntax to older or unknown hosts.
ruleResources.disabledRules: Source-disabled and hide=0 preview rows remain disabled; note text does not affect rule matching.
ruleResources.nativeFlags: fcr and via are emitted only on supported non-FINAL native rules; unsupported FINAL flags fail rather than disappear.

sourceContract.hostUtilities: Explicit flow/info/cnt/dbg return only validated numeric data; ntf controls notices. UA asks native QX to retry once. profile masks select existing remote resources and QR recognizes a subscription URL, both producing a local confirmation action without fetching/importing automatically.

permissions.notifications: Explicit info/flow/cnt/dbg notices contain numeric data only; QR/profile provide a local user-confirmed add-resource action. No credentials, node labels or subscription URLs in notice text. ntf=0 disables notices.

quantumultX.behavior: Atomic offline node/rule/rewrite conversion with the documented helper UI, strict format-aware native semantics and bounded transforms. Registered licensed scripts receive a static API/argument adapter; declarative JSON/header/echo actions are executed and effect-tested. Host import utilities are explicit and require native confirmation. Referenced business scripts are never fetched or executed by the parser.
quantumultX.limitations: Unsupported protocols/transports/security fields, logical/IP/port conjunctions outside the exact positive-domain subset, unbounded or unsupported domain regex, arbitrary script evaluation, CA import, cron and unmapped script APIs fail explicitly. Unknown foreign source parameters are never silently omitted. GEOIP labels require matching database data. Native QX import/device behavior and third-party business-service behavior are not run; native buffering/CPU/empty-body limits remain.
quantumultX.verification: Generated converter/helper and statically compiled licensed runtime execute in restricted VM and Apple JavaScriptCore; loopback HTTP tests verify headers, status and exact text/binary body effects. Four complete original public resources retain URL/hash snapshot checks. Native QX application is not operated.

loon.author: Peng-YM and Sub-Store contributors

sourceContract.input: Loon $resource string, $resourceType number, $resourceUrl string, $loon and optional $argument.
sourceContract.otherTypes: Passed through; not a general plugin/script rewrite converter.

permissions.network: Product can download $resourceUrl if supplied content cannot be converted; shared download utilities may use subscription caches.
permissions.storage: External bundle runs with Loon host privileges and shared download/cache helpers; no wrapper storage or credential setup.

loon.behavior: Parses node and rule resources into Loon format; enable parser-enabled=true on the chosen existing subscription when conversion is needed.
loon.limitations: The recipe references the official AGPL release bundle without redistributing it. No automatic synchronization or Gist upload hook is installed. The upstream build is not claimed to be reproducible.

unsupportedReason: This feature only supplies the documented QX/Loon resource-parser settings. Other clients may use separate Sub-Store or ScriptHub tools; no equivalent parser-key compatibility is claimed.
